sources.text: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside edge of a shape. To find it, add up the lengths of all the sides. The perimeter is measured in ordinary units of length, such as centimetres or metres, not square units. A rectangle with length 7 cm and width 3 cm has a perimeter of 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 cm. We can also use the formula P = 2 x (l + w). For a square, all four sides are equal, so the perimeter is four times the side length. A square with sides of 5 m has a perimeter of 20 m.

A percentage is a number out of 100. The symbol % means "per hundred", so 35% means 35 out of every 100. To find a percentage of an amount, change the percentage into a decimal or a fraction and multiply. For example, to find 20% of 80, write 20% as 0.2 and calculate 0.2 x 80 = 16. A quick way to find 10% of any number is to divide it by 10. To turn a fraction into a percentage, divide the numerator by the denominator and multiply the answer by 100. So 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%.

We can simplify a ratio by dividing both parts by the same number, just like simplifying a fraction. Here both parts divide by 5, so the ratio becomes 2 : 3. history.content: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?

sources.text: Angles are measured in degrees using a protractor. An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees, a right angle is exactly 90 degrees, and an obtuse angle is between 90 and 180 degrees. A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees. The three angles inside any triangle always add up to 180 degrees. So if two angles of a triangle are 50 degrees and 60 degrees, the third angle must be 180 - 50 - 60 = 70 degrees. Angles around a single point add up to 360 degrees, which is one full turn.

history.content: What is the unit of force?

sources.text: A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons (N). Forces can change the speed, direction or shape of an object. Friction is a force that acts between two surfaces that rub together and it always opposes motion. Rough surfaces, such as sandpaper, create a lot of friction, while smooth or oily surfaces create less. Friction is useful because it lets shoes grip the ground and brakes slow down a bike. However, it also wastes energy as heat and causes wear on moving parts, which is why machines are often lubricated with oil.

Matter exists in three main states: solid, liquid and gas. In a solid, the particles are packed tightly in fixed positions and can only vibrate, so a solid keeps its shape. In a liquid, the particles are close together but can slide past each other, so a liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. In a gas, the particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions, so a gas fills any container. Melting changes a solid to a liquid, boiling changes a liquid to a gas, and condensing changes a gas back to a liquid.

history.content: Which planet is closest to the Sun?

sources.text: The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that travels around it. There are eight planets. In order from the Sun they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The four inner planets are small and rocky, while Jupiter and Saturn are giant planets made mostly of gas. Earth takes one year, about 365 days, to orbit the Sun, and it spins once on its axis every 24 hours, which gives us day and night. The Moon is a natural satellite that orbits the Earth about once every month.

history.content: What happens when two north poles of magnets are pushed together?

sources.text: A magnet is an object that attracts certain metals, such as iron, nickel and cobalt. Every magnet has two poles, called the north pole and the south pole. The strongest magnetic force is at the poles. Opposite poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other. So two north poles pushed together will move apart. The area around a magnet where its force can be felt is called its magnetic field. Materials such as plastic, wood and aluminium are not attracted to magnets. A compass needle is a small magnet that lines up with the Earth's magnetic field.

sources.text: An electric circuit is a complete loop that lets electric current flow. A simple circuit needs a power source, such as a cell or battery, wires to carry the current, and a component such as a bulb. If there is a gap anywhere in the loop, the current stops, so a switch works by opening and closing a gap. Materials that let current pass easily, such as copper, are conductors. Materials that do not, such as rubber and plastic, are insulators. In a series circuit there is only one path for the current, while in a parallel circuit there are several branches.

history.content: Which part of a plant cell is NOT found in an animal cell?

sources.text: All living things are made of cells, the tiny building blocks of life. Animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm, a cell membrane and mitochondria. The nucleus controls the activities of the cell. Cytoplasm is the jelly-like liquid where chemical reactions happen. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. Mitochondria release energy from food. Plant cells have all of these parts and also have a cell wall made of cellulose for support, a large vacuole filled with sap, and chloroplasts for photosynthesis. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope.

الجملة الاسمية هي الجملة التي تبدأ باسم. وتتكوّن من ركنين أساسيين هما المبتدأ والخبر. مثال ذلك: «الطالبُ مجتهدٌ» و«السماءُ صافيةٌ». ويكون المبتدأ في الغالب مرفوعًا، وكذلك الخبر. وتدل الجملة الاسمية على الثبات والاستمرار، فهي تصف حال الشيء أو صفته ولا تركّز على حدوث فعل. ويمكن أن يتقدّم الخبر على المبتدأ في بعض الحالات، مثل قولنا: «في الحديقةِ أزهارٌ». وعلينا أن نلاحظ أن الجملة الاسمية تُقرأ من أولها بحثًا عن الاسم الذي بدأت به.

المبتدأ هو الاسم المرفوع الذي تبدأ به الجملة الاسمية، ونتحدث عنه. أما الخبر فهو الجزء الذي يكمل المعنى ويخبرنا عن المبتدأ. في جملة «الكتابُ مفيدٌ» الكتابُ مبتدأ مرفوع وعلامة رفعه الضمة، ومفيدٌ خبر مرفوع كذلك. ويجب أن يطابق الخبر المبتدأ في العدد والنوع، فنقول: «الطالباتُ مجتهداتٌ» ولا نقول «الطالباتُ مجتهدٌ». وقد يكون الخبر مفردًا كما في الأمثلة السابقة، أو جملة، أو شبه جملة مثل الجار والمجرور.

الفاعل هو الاسم المرفوع الذي يدل على من قام بالفعل أو اتصف به. ويأتي بعد الفعل مباشرة. في جملة «نجحَ الطالبُ» الطالبُ هو الفاعل لأنه هو الذي قام بالنجاح، وعلامة رفعه الضمة. وإذا كان الفاعل مثنى رُفع بالألف، مثل «حضرَ الطالبانِ»، وإذا كان جمع مذكر سالمًا رُفع بالواو، مثل «حضرَ المعلمونَ». ويبقى الفعل مفردًا مع الفاعل المثنى والجمع، فنقول «حضرَ الطالبانِ» ولا نقول «حضرا الطالبانِ».

sources.text: المفعول به هو اسم منصوب يدل على من وقع عليه فعل الفاعل. نسأل عنه بقولنا: ماذا؟ أو من؟ بعد الفعل والفاعل. في جملة «قرأَ الولدُ القصةَ» نسأل: ماذا قرأ الولد؟ فيكون الجواب القصةَ، وهي مفعول به منصوب وعلامة نصبه الفتحة. وإذا كان المفعول به مثنى نُصب بالياء، مثل «رأيتُ الطالبينِ»، وإذا كان جمع مؤنث سالمًا نُصب بالكسرة، مثل «شاهدتُ المعلماتِ». وقد يكون المفعول به ضميرًا متصلًا كما في «أكرمتُهُ».

كان وأخواتها أفعال ناقصة تدخل على الجملة الاسمية، فترفع المبتدأ ويسمى اسمها، وتنصب الخبر ويسمى خبرها. ومن أخواتها: أصبح، وأمسى، وظلّ، وبات، وصار، وليس. مثال ذلك: «كان الجوُّ جميلًا». فالجوُّ اسم كان مرفوع، وجميلًا خبرها منصوب وعلامة نصبه الفتحة. وتدل كان على حدوث الشيء في الزمن الماضي، أما «ليس» فتدل على نفي الحال، مثل «ليس الكسولُ ناجحًا». وتسمى هذه الأفعال ناقصة لأنها لا تكتفي باسمها بل تحتاج إلى الخبر لتتم الفائدة.

sources.text: The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that travels around it. There are eight planets. In order from the Sun they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. The four inner planets are small and rocky, while Jupiter and Saturn are giant planets made mostly of gas. Earth takes one year, about 365 days, to orbit the Sun, and it spins once on its axis every 24 hours, which gives us day and night. The Moon is a natural satellite that orbits the Earth about once every month.
